question.text: Industry best practice in Ch 11.11 recommends the Manager set up a Supervisory Committee that meets at least:

answer.text: Once a year, covering valuation of assets exceeding the pre-defined maximum investment per Company, governance issues, terms/conditions of the Fund, and resolution of potential conflicts
Only upon LP request, with no minimum frequency

explanation.text: The Logic: Per Ch 11.11 (Industry best practices, Governance), the Manager can set up a Supervisory Committee that meets AT LEAST ONCE A YEAR. Its powers generally comprise valuation of assets exceeding pre-defined maximums per Company, governance issues, fund terms/conditions, and resolution of potential conflicts of interest. Committee resolutions cannot replace mandatory investor consent. The Trap: Weekly/monthly frequencies are impractical and not industry norm. Option D provides no discipline. Cross-Exam Context: Governance best practices tested across XIX-A, XIX-C. Manager's Pro-Tip: Supplement the annual Supervisory Committee meeting with ad-hoc triggers: any transaction above X% of NAV, any related-party query, any LP complaint escalation. This keeps the Committee engaged between annual meetings.
